committee: CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board
overview: The CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board serves as a municipal bank and policy body dedicated to creating and preserving affordable housing in Medford. Established in August 2024, the board oversees the distribution of housing funds, evaluates city-owned land for development, and implements strategic housing plans. The body has spent its initial years establishing governance structures, securing Community Preservation Act funding, and drafting a five-year Action Plan. Most recently, the board has been finalizing standardized developer application templates, preparing for its first housing resource fair, and advancing ordinance language for housing linkage fees.

threads.name: Governance and Foundational Documents
threads.summary: In its inaugural 2024 meetings, the board established officer roles and formed working groups to draft a Declaration of Trust and a strategic action plan. Members received statutory training from the Massachusetts Housing Partnership to define the trust's legal powers and eligible expenditures. The board formally executed the Declaration of Trust in January 2025, enabling the document to be recorded with the Registry of Deeds. Later meetings focused on administrative updates, including transitioning funds to accessible special revenue accounts and managing trustee term expirations.

threads.name: Five-Year Affordable Housing Action Plan
threads.summary: The board initiated a multi-phase strategic planning process in late 2024 to identify housing needs and establish measurable goals. Planning involved reviewing demographic data that showed local housing costs significantly outpaced median wages, alongside several stakeholder focus groups and public workshops. A draft five-year action plan was presented for public comment in July 2025, outlining goals for partnerships with mission-driven developers and the Medford Housing Authority. The board officially approved the final version of the plan in October 2025 for submission to the City Council.

threads.name: CPA Funding and Revenue Streams
threads.summary: The trust relies on various funding sources, primarily through recurring applications to the Community Preservation Committee (CPC). After receiving an initial $250,000 in Community Preservation Act (CPA) funds in early 2025, the board successfully petitioned for additional fiscal year 2026 funds totaling $550,000. Other revenue strategies explored include real estate transfer fees, payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) from institutions, and the sale of underutilized municipal land. In late 2026, the board noted the completion of a linkage fee nexus study, which is the precursor to drafting a local ordinance to generate further revenue.

threads.name: Developer Application and Grant Process
threads.summary: To distribute funds, the board developed a formal application process and guidelines for housing developers. Initial discussions focused on creating a periodic Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), but the board later moved toward a rolling application process to better align with developer timelines. In 2026, the board continued refining standardized application templates to improve the capture of 20-year operating budgets and project cost categories. As of September 2026, the board is anticipating a new funding request from the Medford Housing Authority for the Walkman Court project.

threads.name: 703 Fellsway West Project
threads.summary: The board evaluated its first major funding request for an affordable housing project at 703 Fellsway West, sponsored by Metro Community Housing. The developer initially requested $200,000 to cover utility-related delays and inflationary overruns, which the board reduced to a $100,000 loan after negotiations. In 2026, the board discovered that the original loan documents had not been properly recorded at the Registry of Deeds. This led to ongoing discussions regarding legal remedies and conditions that must be met before executing additional funding for the property.

threads.name: Zoning Reforms and Fractional Payments
threads.summary: The board actively engages with the city's zoning overhaul to ensure new regulations support affordability goals. A major focus has been establishing a system for 'fractional payments,' allowing developers to pay a fee to the trust instead of rounding up to a full affordable unit. While a resolution for these payments was proposed in late 2025, the formula required revisions in 2026 after state-level metric changes. Most recently, the board reviewed standardized calculation spreadsheets to maximize these payments and ensure zoning incentive bonuses deliver deep affordability.

threads.name: Public Outreach and Housing Resources
threads.summary: The trust coordinates public engagement to educate residents on available housing resources and the board's activities. Beyond statutory public hearings for the Action Plan, the board partnered with CHAPA for technical assistance and outreach materials. In 2026, the board initiated plans for a community housing resource fair and a fundraising campaign. Originally planned for June, the fair was moved to the fall to allow for more planning regarding marketing, panel speakers, and informational flyers.
